finding.claim: OS command injection in GET /ping. The `host` query parameter is concatenated into a shell command string and run with child_process.exec, which spawns a shell. An attacker can append shell metacharacters (`;`, `&&`, `|`, `$()`, backticks) to run arbitrary commands as the server user. The command output is returned in the response, so the attacker sees the results directly.
finding.source: req.query.host, the HTTP GET /ping query parameter. It is unauthenticated and the server listens on port 3001 on all interfaces by default.
finding.sink: child_process.exec("ping -c 1 " + req.query.host) at tools.js:7, which runs through /bin/sh -c.

trace.note: Route handler for GET /ping receives req with attacker-controlled query string
req.query.host is concatenated unsanitized into the command string passed to exec()
stdout is returned via res.send(out), so command output is exfiltrated to the attacker. An error returns 502 with no body.
app.listen(3001) binds to all interfaces, so the route is network-reachable

finding.guards_checked: No input validation, allowlist, or hostname/IP regex on `host`. No authentication or authorization middleware (no app.use calls). No rate limiting. The value is not passed through execFile with an argument array, which would avoid the shell. A leading `-` in `host` could also inject ping options. No reverse-proxy or network restriction appears in the repo. The other routes are not exploitable: /version (line 16) uses execFile with a fixed argument array and no user input, and /uptime (line 25) runs a constant command.

verdict.reason: tools.js:7 concatenates req.query.host into exec() (shell) with no validation, auth middleware, or execFile, and tools.js:11 returns stdout. Output is returned when the exit status is 0, e.g. `x; id`. app.listen(3001) at tools.js:28 is reachable by an anonymous attacker.
